description.narrative: Stödet som är ett kärnstöd för implementering av Mama Cash:s strategisk plan 2009-2013. Planen omfattar följande komponenter: 1)stöd till mindre och medelstor kvinnorättsorganisationer; 2) kvinnorättsfonder; samt 3) kommunikation och resursmobilisering. I förslaget ingår även att stärka Mama Cash som organisation.

The core support is for implementation of MamaCash's strategic plan 2009-2013. The plan covers the following components: 1) Fund and support women's & girls' human rights organisations; 2) Build a strong global architecture of women's funds; and 3) Communicate their core message, and promote women's and girls' rights, learning, and community-building. Organisational dev is also part of the plan.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative: General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Mama Cash´s vision and mission relates to increasing women and girls power and resources in order for them to be able to participate fully and equally in creating a peaceful, just and sustainable world. Guided by Mama Cash values and though partnership funding, networking and capacity building are the core of Mama Cash´s work and outcomes. The stated intervention logic (above) with three grant objectives is assessed by Sida as achieved. 1) I.e. during Mama Cash launched a new organisation-wide Learning, Monitoring and Evaluation (LME) framework, 2) i.e through Sida´s overall support Mama Cash managed to distribute 3 636 900 Euro in 111 grants to 100 different groups in 61 countries worldwide (grants to Body, Money, Voice, Women´s Funds Portfolios, Strategic Partnership grants, Opportunity Fund grants and Red Umbrella Fund grants). 3) Mama Cash together with Association for Women´s Rights in Development (AWID) have a partnership with the Guardian aimed at amplifying the voice of women´s rights advocates. I.e. in 2015, 233 items were published in the Guardian related to the partnership (compared to 166 in 2014).
